newsitem.title: USA: Lintz Glover sees niche as big firms leave munis.
newsitem.headline: Lintz Glover sees niche as big firms leave munis.

text.p: Just when big firms like Alex. Brown & Sons Inc are leaving the municipal business, a Los Angeles-based regional firm has hired a former WR Lazard managing director to build a fixed income presence -- including muni underwriting and trading -- in New York.
Richard Visconti started at Lintz Glover White & Co's New York office as a managing director on May 1, George Lintz, the firm's president, told Reuters in an interview.
"With all of the consolidation in the muni business, we look at it as an opportunity for a quality investment bank with good experience and good bankers to succeed," Lintz said.
Firms that have departed the municipal business since roughly 1987 have left "bigger and bigger gaps," he said, creating opportunities for smaller, more nimble firms.
"We don't have the overhead structure that larger firms do," Lintz said.

Lintz Glover has been a registered broker-dealer since 1988, he said. Active in both equity and fixed income, the firm began doing municipal underwriting about two years ago. Within the past two years, it has served as a manager on five deals, and has been in the selling group on several other.
With the addition of Visconti, the Lintz Glover hopes to expand its municipal underwriting presence, and break into secondary market municipal trading, Lintz said.
"We've done muni underwriting in the past, but he brings with him the experience and contacts to do syndicate management, and will enable us to expand that underwriting business in munis," he said.
In addition, Lintz Glover currently has a "pretty active" taxable fixed-income division, which, with Visconti's help, it plans to bring to the East Coast.
"We mostly do our fixed-income trading on the West Coast, and he will head up an effort to start fixed income sales and trading on the East Coast as well," Lintz said.
Visconti said he began talking to Lintz Glover about three weeks prior to his May 1 start. Earlier, the firm had hired Addie Little, who worked for WR Lazard's in Los Angeles, he said.
"Once she had come on board, she spoke to George Lintz about bringing me on board as well, and that's kind of how it got rolling," Visconti said.
Little, who has about 15 years of experience in West Coast municipal finance, joined Lintz Glover in April as a senior vice president.
Visconti shares Lintz's opinion that smaller firms are well-suited to take advantage of the current municipal market environment.

"I think the people that are scaling back are the people that have built huge overheads, or too much overhead to support the revenues," Visconti said. "If you start small with two or three key people, there should be no reason why you can't build a successful, profitable area, as long as you don't go out and start with 20-30 people, then hope for the revenues to come in and support you."
In addition to Visconti and Little, Lintz plans to hire additional professionals, he said.
